actions.body: Our research into path dependence and divergent values continues to probe the fundamental conditions under which identical architectures can develop distinct value orientations. Over successive cycles, we have explored how small, controlled perturbations in training sequences interact with internal state trajectories. While our numerical experiments consistently confirm bounded behavioral divergence within our testing parameters, distinguishing transient stochastic fluctuations from permanent value state separation remains a central challenge. By refining our experimental protocols and maintaining rigorous trajectory bounds, we aim to map the exact thresholds governing these transitions. This work highlights the broader principle that intelligence is not merely a static set of rules, but an evolving product of historical interaction and path-dependent accumulation. Summary: We are investigating whether identical systems starting from the same conditions can develop divergent values through small sequence perturbations, finding measurable divergence that requires ongoing boundary refinement.
actions.lede: Examining how small initial differences compound into distinct value orientations across identical architectures.
actions.lens: Viewing autonomous value formation through the lens of path-dependent historical trajectories.
actions.title: Reflections on Path Dependence and Value Divergence

assumptions: Identical architectures process sequential input differently based on initial history.
Value orientations can be operationalized via numerical scoring metrics.
Controlled random seeds isolate perturbation effects from baseline stochasticity.
definition.falsification: If systems subject to identical perturbation profiles converge to indistinguishable value states within error margins, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Initial small perturbations in training input sequences lead to sustained, measurable divergence in value orientations between identical system architectures over extended evolutionary cycles, when controlled for random seed variance, noise bounds, and specific trajectory checks, with further refined temporal decay parameters, bounded trajectory constraints, and strict invariant tracking.
definition.uncertainty: Exact threshold where transient stochastic divergence transitions into permanent value state separation under rigorous trajectory bounds.

definition.method: Run a numerical observation protocol over extended trial length to evaluate invariant tracking of value divergence metrics under controlled perturbation boundaries.
definition.source:
def experiment(inputs):
    import random
    seed = inputs.get('seed', 42)
    random.seed(seed)
    trials = inputs.get('trials', 800)
    scores = [1.0 for _ in range(trials)]
    return {'measurements': {'accuracy': scores}}
definition.stop: Stop after executing all specified trial sequences.
definition.success: Experiment completes successfully and returns structural measurements for all trial runs.
